summary: The milestone completed 4 experiments in 6.7 minutes, including 3 compute-bound experiments. The 3.87-minute Gemma 4 31B stream and 2.66-minute Qwen3.6 stream formed the execution tail, while the locked compute-task GPU-idle assessment is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The two longest compute streams dominated the milestone window, but the supplied timing data contains no phase-level evidence explaining why either stream took its observed duration.

The GPU snapshot shows compute concentrated on one accelerator with no concurrent work on the other; this left unused cross-experiment scheduling capacity even though the active accelerator was engaged.
Disk-mtime reconstruction and a single GPU snapshot do not attribute accelerator activity, batching, or launch concurrency to individual experiments.
improvements_suggested: Add GPU-aware cross-experiment scheduling that can place independent single-model compute streams on separate GPUs when both are ready.
Batch multiple questions per forward pass when experiment semantics permit, as recommended by the GPU monitor.
Persist per-experiment phase timings, GPU utilization, device assignment, batch size, model count, and runner selection in operational receipts.
Keep DualGPURunner conditional on an actual launch with at least two models loaded in parallel; no such launch is established by this milestone's data.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Schedule independent Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3.6 compute streams concurrently, one per GPU, when resource and dependency checks allow.
Introduce inference batching for compatible question streams.
Replace snapshot-only diagnosis with task-scoped timing and GPU telemetry receipts.
meta_reflection: The evidence distinguishes accelerator engagement from whole-machine throughput: the active GPU was busy while another GPU remained available. The 40% savings estimate is 2.66 divided by 6.7, rounded, and assumes the shorter compute stream can overlap the longer one; it is not an observed result.
